content: The L1 family is a group of cell adhesion molecules that includes various L1-like proteins. These proteins are present in the nervous system and other tissues across many animal species. They are expressed on radial glial cells and play a critical role in neural cell migration during developmental processes. In humans, the members of the L1 family are known as L1, CHL1 (close homolog of L1), Neurofascin, and NrCAM (NgCAM-related cell adhesion molecule). A defining feature of this family is their ability to bind to a group of proteins called ankyrins. Both NrCAM and Neurofascin possess class 1 PDZ domain-binding motifs at their COOH termini. NrCAM, in particular, has the ability to bind to SAP102 and other members of the MAGUK (membrane-associated guanylate kinase) family.
